_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-15 · Sky159 — all three Admin requests are built; nobody has tried them in a real browser yet.
_status:
Everything you asked for on the Admin tab last night is now built. The hide button no longer toggles silently — it ASKS who should see the item, as one list from "Everyone" down to "nobody". Every menu item now shows what actually protects its data, not just the alarming ones (only 1 item in 7 was labelled before). And you can create your own menu categories and drag items into them. The Memory tab fix you said was fine to leave is also in — it was a real locked door, not just an inconvenience.

None of it has been tried in a real browser. The sandbox cannot reach the site, so the whole list below rests on one round trip that only you can do. That is the top item, and it has been the top item for two sessions.

items.text: Three questions for Jenni, in one go. (1) Confirm the Basic Skills code pairing — this single answer unblocks the first three build phases of the noncredit CIP work. (2) Two codes are in real use but missing from her list: 32.0199 (60 programs) and 35.0101 (16). (3) The big one: can a non-CDCP category be CTE at all? That decides roughly 1,300 programs, and CTE is funding-bearing.

Decide where a confirmed noncredit category gets saved. Right now the plan was the browser's own storage, which is wrong for something that affects funding — it vanishes on another machine and nobody can see who decided what. Recommend a proper table that records who confirmed it and when.

Make the COBI header accessible and mobile-friendly, and drop the superscript from the logo. The superscript C is genuinely impossible — Unicode has no superscript capital C, so "CPL" renders as "cPL" and no font fixes it. Sam's call: plain, unbolded org name instead.

Sam wants to edit the Project Description in the ℹ About menu — it has gone stale as the project grew. It can't be edited in the page: the daily job rewrites that block every morning. The editor has to change where the daily job READS the description from.

Six new decision rights are on the register with nobody's name against them. Start with DR-13, the workplan itself — it is the most public thing the project publishes, four of its tables can be edited in the page by anyone holding the team phrase, and a wrong figure reaches the live dashboard on the next morning's run.

Sierra named 1 of 9 D1.1 welding credentials and nobody has worked out why yet. Measure first: either the search never returned the other eight, or it found them and the answer only mentioned the best one. Those are different bugs with different fixes.

The one test that proves the last three sessions of work. Sign in with the magic link from the ℹ About menu — it opens a NEW browser tab. Go back to your ORIGINAL tab: it should be signed in too. Then on Admin, drag a menu item and press Save — you should see "✓ Saved.", not an error. Leave it an hour, come back, open a team tab: it should not say you are signed out. Finally sign out, and check BOTH tabs stay signed out. If anything misbehaves, say which step.

Try making a menu category. Type a name, press "+ Add category", drag two items into it, press Save, then reload the page. Then empty it out and press the 🗑 button, Save, and reload again — it should stay gone. If it comes back after you deleted it, that is a real failure and worth reporting.

Check the new visibility control reads the way you meant. Pressing it now ASKS who should see the item rather than just hiding it, and each choice says what it does. If you only ever wanted to NOTE that a team phrase is needed, the answer is to leave it on "Everyone" — the tab already tells people when they open it. Tell us if that still reads wrong.

The project's always-loaded instructions file is still twice the size it should be. This session archived one old session write-up and rewrote a section instead of adding to it, but that is holding the line, not fixing it. The finished workstreams — the EACR filters, the team phrases, the sign-in work — are history now and belong in the reference folder. Every line costs every future session.
